 The Cabinet makes the following Regulations under Sections 40(1)(j) and 62 of the
 Environmental Management and Climate Change Act 2020.

 PART 1 — PRELIMINARY

 1 Citation
 These Regulations may be cited as the Environmental Management and Climate
 Change (Climate Change and Environment Protection Fund) Regulations 2026.

 2 Commencement
 These Regulations come into effect on the day they are notified in the Gazette.

 3 Interpretation
 In these Regulations, unless inconsistent with the context or subject matter:
 ‘Chief Administrative Officer’ means a person appointed under Regulation 16;
 ‘Custodian Bank’ means the bank referred to in Regulation 21;
 ‘Endowment Account’ means the account required to be opened under
 Regulation 22(1)(a);
 ‘Fund’ means the National Climate Change and Environment Protection Fund
 established by Part 9 of the Environmental Management and Climate Change
 Act 2020;
 ‘Guidelines’ means the guidelines for Fund operations approved by the
 Managing Committee;
 ‘Managing Committee’ means the Committee established under Part 2;
 ‘international organisation’ means an international organisation referred to in
 Section 40(2)(b) of the Act;
 ‘Operating Account’ means the account required to be opened under Regulation
 22(1)(b);
 ‘public enterprise’ has the meaning given to it under the Public Enterprise Act
 2019;
 ‘Supervisory Committee’ means the supervisory committee established under
 Regulation 9; and
 ‘Technical Working Committee’ means a committee established under
 Regulation 12.

 4 Purpose of the Regulations
 These Regulations prescribe matters necessary to implement the Fund.

 5 Purposes of the Fund
 For the purposes of Section 40(1)(j) of the Act, the Fund is also established to:
 (a) improve resilience to climate change through adaptation and mitigation
 measures;

 (c) ensure climate change information is available to end-users.

 PART 2 — COMMITTEES OF THE FUND

 6 Establishment of the Managing Committee
 (1) There shall be a Managing Committee for the Fund.
 (2) The ex officio members of the Managing Committee are the:
 (a) Secretary for Environmental Management and Agriculture;
 (b) Secretary for Climate Change and National Resilience; and
 (c) Secretary for Finance.
 (3) The Managing Committee may recommend that the Minister appoint
 additional members including representatives of:
 (a) a public enterprise; or
 (b) an international organisation.
 (4) The term of appointment of:
 (a) an ex officio member shall be the duration of time that he or she holds
 office in the position; and
 (b) a member appointed under subregulation (3) shall not exceed 3
 consecutive years.
 (5) Except as otherwise provided under the Act or these Regulations, members
 of the Managing Committee shall be in a fiduciary relationship to the Fund
 and shall exercise powers and functions under these Regulations:
 (a) in good faith; and
 (b) with reasonable care and diligence.
 (6) Members of the Managing Committee are presumed to exercise powers and
 functions under these Regulations in good faith and with reasonable care
 and diligence unless the contrary is proved.

 7 Functions of the Managing Committee
 (1) The Managing Committee shall manage the Fund in accordance with the
 Act, these Regulations and the Guidelines.
 (2) Without limiting subregulation (1), the Managing Committee has the
 following functions:
 (a) approve Guidelines for the Fund;
 (b) submit annual projections of income and expenses to the Department of
 Finance in accordance with Regulation 30;
 (c) approve or reject project funding applications in accordance with
 Regulation 38;
 (d) make all necessary arrangements for investment of the Fund in
 accordance with Regulation 24;
 (e) provide reports, updates and other information to the Supervisory
 Committee as requested, in accordance with Regulation 10;
 (f) advise on any matter for the purposes of meeting the objectives of the
 Fund;
 (g) appoint officers and staff in accordance with Regulations 16, 17, and
 18;
 (h) delegate powers and functions to Officers in accordance with the Act,
 these Regulations, and the Guidelines;

 (i) establish Technical Working Groups in accordance with Regulation 12;
 (j) appoint a Custodian Bank in accordance with Regulation 21;
 (k) approve and implement an investment policy in accordance with
 Regulation 24;
 (l) approve withdrawals from the Fund following authorisation by Cabinet
 in accordance with the Act and Regulation 26;
 (m) evaluate and approve grant applications in accordance with Regulations
 38 and 39;
 (n) suspend or terminate a project in accordance with Regulation 40;
 (o) enter into contracts, and commence or defend legal proceedings, on
 behalf of the Fund; and
 (p) do all such other things as are incidental or conducive to the fulfilment
 of the purposes of the Fund.

8 Powers of the Managing Committee
 The Managing Committee has the power to do all things necessary or
 convenient for the performance of its functions.

9 Establishment of the Supervisory Committee
 (1) There shall be a Supervisory Committee for the Fund.
 (2) The ex officio members of the Supervisory Committee are the:
 (a) Minister for Environmental Management and Agriculture;
 (b) Minister for Climate Change and National Resilience; and
 (c) Minister for Finance.

10 Functions of the Supervisory Committee
 (1) The Supervisory Committee shall provide oversight of the Fund in
 accordance with the Act, these Regulations, and the Guidelines.
 (2) Without limiting subregulation (1), the Supervisory Committee has the
 following functions:
 (a) approve the annual projections of income and expenses as well as the
 annual report of the Fund;
 (b) provide recommendations to the Managing Committee on Fund
 priorities, coordination of Fund activities, and improvements to Fund
 performance;
 (c) obtain reports, updates and other information from the Managing
 Committee;
 (d) require changes to the annual projections of income and expenses as
 well as the annual report of the Fund;
 (e) commission strategic reviews of the Fund as appropriate; and
 (f) take any action necessary or convenient for the performance of
 oversight functions under these Regulations.

11 Powers of the Supervisory Committee
 (1) The Supervisory Committee has the power to do all things necessary or
 convenient for the performance of its functions.
 (2) The Supervisory Committee shall not exercise powers vested in the
 Managing Committee.

 12 Establishment of Technical Working Committee
 (1) The Managing Committee shall establish Technical Working Committees to
 assess project applications under Part 5 of these Regulations.
 (2) Technical Working Committees shall in accordance with Regulations 37
 and 38:
 (a) evaluate and assess project applications; and
 (b) provide recommendations on project applications to the Managing
 Committee.
 (3) The Guidelines shall prescribe the procedures for the Managing Committee
 to appoint expert members of Technical Working Committees.

 13 Meetings and Quorum
 (1) The Managing Committee shall conduct its meetings in the manner that is
 determined by the Managing Committee.
 (2) The Supervisory Committee shall conduct its meetings in the manner that is
 determined by the Supervisory Committee.
 (3) The Technical Working Committee shall conduct its meetings in the manner
 that is determined by the Managing Committee.
 (4) If a member is unable to attend a meeting of any Committee established
 under these Regulations, the member may designate a Proxy to represent
 the absent member in the meeting.
 (5) In relation to the quorums of the Committees:
 (a) all members of the Managing Committee, Supervisory Committee,
 inclusive of designated Proxies, shall constitute a quorum for the
 purposes of meetings; and
 (b) the quorum for a Technical Working Committee is a majority of its
 members, inclusive of designated Proxies.
 (6) Decisions of a Committee established under these Regulations shall be
 made by consensus.
 (7) The Chief Administrative Officer shall ensure that proper minutes are
 recorded and maintained in respect of all meetings of a Committee
 established under these Regulations.
 (8) The rules of procedure of each Committee established under these
 Regulations shall be prescribed in the Guidelines.

 14 Conflicts of Interest
 (1) The members of a Committee established under these Regulations is not
 entitled to receive payment, allowance or remuneration for the performance
 of functions or exercise of powers under the Act, these Regulations, or the
 Guidelines.
 (2) A member of a committee established under these Regulations who has,
 directly or indirectly, a financial or personal interest in any matter before the
 Committee shall declare his or her interest in the matter prior to a meeting.
 (3) A member of a Committee established under these Regulations who has,
 directly or indirectly, a financial or personal interest in any matter before the
 Committee shall not with respect to that matter:
 (a) be present during deliberations by the Committee; and

 (b) participate in or vote on such matter.
 (4) The exclusion of a Committee member under subregulation (3) shall be
 disregarded for the purposes of constituting a quorum under Regulation
 13(5).
 (5) The decisions of a Committee made in contravention of subregulation (3)
 shall be void and have no legal effect.

15 Protection from Liability
 The members of a Committee established under these Regulations shall not be
 liable for any loss or damage arising from, or be subject to, any criminal
 prosecution and civil claims for the performance of a function or duty or
 exercise of a power in good faith under the Act, or any other written law.

 PART 3 — OFFICERS OF THE FUND

 16 Chief Administrative Officer
 (1) The Chief Secretary shall appoint a Chief Administrative Officer in
 consultation with the Managing Committee.
 (2) The terms and conditions of the employment of the Chief Administrative
 Officer shall be regulated under the Public Service Act 2016.
 (3) The Chief Administrative Officer is accountable to the Managing
 Committee and is responsible for the administration of the Fund.
 (4) Without limiting subregulation (2), the Chief Administrative Officer has the
 following functions:
 (a) convene Committee meetings at the request of the Chairperson;
 (b) provide administrative support for Committee meetings;
 (c) prepare annual projections of income and expenses as well as the
 annual report of the Fund;
 (d) coordinate and facilitate the implementation of Managing Committee
 decisions;
 (e) assist in the selection and supervision of the Custodian Bank; and
 (f) liaise with project applicants and implementers.

 17 Accounting Officer
 (1) The Chief Secretary shall appoint an Accounting Officer in consultation
 with the Managing Committee.
 (2) The Accounting Officer is accountable to the Chief Administrative Officer
 and shall provide financial support services to the Managing Committee.
 (3) The terms and conditions of the employment of the Accounting Officer shall
 be regulated under the Public Service Act 2016.
 (4) Without limiting subregulation (3), the Accounting Officer has the following
 functions:
 (a) receive transfers to the Fund;
 (b) ensure Fund moneys are deposited into one of the bank accounts
 prescribed in Regulations 22 and 23; and
 (c) approve payments and disbursements from the Fund for authorisation
 by the Managing Committee.
 (5) The Managing Committee may delegate record-keeping powers and
 functions to the Accounting Officer, to be performed in accordance with
 Regulation 30.

 18 Appointment of Other Staff
 The Chief Secretary in consultation with the Managing Committee, may appoint
 any other staff of the Fund for the proper and efficient performance of the
 objectives of the Fund.

 19 Delegations
 (1) The Managing Committee may delegate any of its powers and functions
 under these Regulations to any officer of the Fund, except the power of
 delegation.

 PART 4 — FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND REPORTING

 20 Fund Management and Bank Accounts
 (1) The Managing Committee shall maintain bank accounts of the Fund in
 accordance with these Regulations.
 (2) All moneys payable to the Fund under the Act, these Regulations, or any
 Donor agreement must be deposited into bank accounts of the Fund in
 accordance with these Regulations.

 21 Custodian Bank
 (1) The Managing Committee shall appoint a Custodian Bank for the Fund that:
 (a) is an existing financial institution in Australia;
 (b) has a net worth in excess of AUD 100 million;
 (c) has at least 10 years of experience as a custodian of financial assets;
 and
 (d) is capable of providing financial services in Naoero.
 (2) The Custodian Bank shall maintain full and accurate records of income,
 expenditure, and transactions of the Fund.
 (3) The Guidelines shall set out further requirements for the agreement between
 the Fund and the Custodian Bank.

 22 Endowment and Operating Accounts
 (1) The Managing Committee shall with the written authorisation of the
 Minister for Finance, direct the Accounting Officer to open 2 accounts at the
 Custodian Bank as follows:
 (a) an Endowment Account; and
 (b) an Operating Account.
 (2) The Endowment Account under subregulation (1)(a) shall consist of funds
 provided under Section 40(2) of the Act.
 (3) The Operating Account under subregulation (1)(b) shall consist of:
 (a) funds available for operational expenses including procurements under
 Part 3A of the Public Finance (Control and Management) Act 1997;
 and
 (b) funds allocated for approved projects by the Managing Committee
 pursuant to Part 5 of these Regulations.
 (4) The Guidelines shall set out rules and procedures for the Endowment and
 Operating Accounts of the Fund.

 23 Sinking Account
 (1) Upon agreement with an international organisation and with the written
 authorisation of the Minister for Finance, the Managing Committee may
 direct the accounting officer to open at the Custodian bank:
 (a) a sinking account; and
 (b) sub-accounts of the sinking account.

 (2) The sinking account and its sub-accounts may consist of grants, donations
 or contributions from international organisations, pursuant to Section
 40(2)(b) of the Act.
 (3) Monies in a sinking account or sub-account may be subject to any condition
 set out in agreements between the Fund and an international organisation.
 (4) The Guidelines shall set out further requirements for sinking accounts of the
 Fund.

24 Investment Policy
 (1) The Managing Committee shall develop an investment policy for
 investment of funds in the Endowment Account established under these
 Regulations.
 (2) The Managing Committee may appoint investment advisers through a
 competitive tender process to assist in the development of an investment
 policy under subregulation (1).
 (3) Investment advisers appointed pursuant to subregulation (2) shall be
 obliged to exercise integrity, prudence and professional skill in fulfilling
 functions delegated to them by the Management Committee.
 (4) The investment policy referred to in subregulation (1) shall ensure that the
 Endowment Account of the Fund is invested in low-risk financial
 instruments that protect capital and maintain adequate liquidity for
 operations of the Fund.
 (5) Moneys payable to the Fund shall not be withdrawn from the Endowment
 Account other than in accordance with these Regulations and any
 investment policy established pursuant to subregulation (1).

25 Restrictions on Use of Fund Monies
 (1) The Fund assets and monies shall not be withdrawn, disbursed, or disposed
 of in any manner other than in accordance with the Act and these
 Regulations.
 (2) The Managing Committee and Supervisory Committee shall ensure the
 Fund assets and monies are not used to lend, borrow, mortgage or otherwise
 charge the assets of the Fund.
 (3) The Managing Committee and Supervisory Committee shall ensure not to
 use more than 30% of the Operating Account to meet operational expenses
 of the Fund including procurements under Part 3A of the Public Finance
 (Control and Management) Act 1997.

26 Withdrawals from the Fund
 (1) The Managing Committee shall ensure that no withdrawal is made or
 authorised from the Fund unless the:
 (a) withdrawal is for the purpose for which the Fund is established; and
 (b) purpose of the withdrawal has been authorised by the Cabinet in
 consultation with the Minister.
 (2) For the purpose of Section 41(2) of the Act, the Managing Committee shall
 authorise withdrawals from the Fund prior to signature by the Secretary for
 Environmental Management and Agriculture, Secretary for Climate Change
 and National Resilience and the Secretary for Finance.

 (3) Withdrawals from the Endowment Account may only be made to the
 Operating Account in accordance with the approved annual projections of
 the Fund under Regulation 30.
 (4) Subject to the Act and these Regulations, the Management Committee shall
 develop a withdrawal policy for approval by the Supervisory Committee.

 27 Payments and Disbursements
 (1) Payments and disbursements from the Fund shall be made in a manner
 consistent with the Act and these Regulations, the Public Finance Control
 and Management Act 1997, and the Public Finance (Control and
 Management) Regulations 2013.
 (2) The Guidelines may set out further procedures for payments and
 disbursements from the Fund pursuant to subregulation (1).

 28 Return of Unspent Funds
 Where grant monies under Part 5 of these Regulations have not been spent:
 (a) at the completion of the project; or
 (b) due to the termination of the project pursuant to Regulation 40,
 the Managing Committee shall direct in writing that the unspent money be
 returned and deposited into either the Endowment Account or the Operating
 Account.

 29 Financial Record-Keeping
 (1) Where the Secretary delegates his or her functions under Section 42(1) of
 the Act to the Managing Committee, the Managing Committee shall:
 (a) ensure that all payments, disbursements, and withdrawals of Fund
 monies are recorded in accordance with the Public Finance (Control
 and Management) Act 1997 and the Public Finance (Control and
 Management) Regulations 2013; and
 (b) keep written financial records that:
 (i) record the transactions, financial position and performance of the
 Fund;
 (ii) enable financial statements to be prepared and audited in
 accordance with the Act and these Regulations;
 (iii) enable other reports required by these Regulations to be prepared;
 and
 (iv) comply with any additional record-keeping requirements specified
 in an agreement between the Fund and an international
 organisation.
 (2) The records required under subregulation (1)(b):
 (a) must be kept for at least 7 years after the most recent transaction to
 which they relate; and
 (b) may be kept in electronic form that are readily retrievable and
 convertible into physical copy.

 30 Annual Projections
 (1) The Managing Committee shall submit annual projections of income and
 expenditure of the Fund to the Department of Finance after approval by the
 Supervisory Committee.

 (2) The annual projections referred to in subregulation (1) shall include
 estimates of:
 (a) moneys payable to the Fund under Section 40(2) of the Act;
 (b) operational expenses of the Fund;
 (c) expenditure on grants under Part 5 of these Regulations; and
 (d) transfers from the Endowment Account to the Operations Account.
 (3) The annual projections referred to in subregulation (1) shall be tabled:
 (a) before the start of the financial year; or
 (b) if Parliament, by resolution, determines a later date for the tabling of
 the annual projections for the financial year, by the later date.

31 Annual Report
 (1) The Managing Committee shall provide an annual report, approved by the
 Supervisory Committee, in order to meet reporting requirements to the
 Cabinet pursuant to Section 42(2)(a) of the Act.
 (2) The annual report shall include for the financial year to which it relates:
 (a) the financial statement set out in Regulation 32(2);
 (b) the number and nature of projects approved, including the amount of
 Fund monies allocated;
 (c) the status of all ongoing and completed projects;
 (d) for each reportable deviation from the annual projections approved
 under Regulation 30, whether previously reported or not, specify the
 reason for the deviation; and
 (e) a statement on the extent to which the Managing Committee believes
 the Fund has achieved one or more of the purposes set out in Section
 40(1) of the Act and Regulation 5.
 (3) The Minister of Finance shall table in Parliament the annual report referred
 to in subregulation (1) and (2):
 (a) within 2 sitting days after the end of the financial year; or
 (b) if Parliament, by resolution, determines a later date for the tabling of
 the annual report for the financial year, by the later date.

32 Financial Statement
 (1) The Managing Committee shall provide an annual financial statement,
 approved by the Supervisory Committee, in order to meet reporting
 requirements to the Auditor General under Section 42(2)(b) of the Act.
 (2) The financial statement in subregulation (1) shall include the following
 information regarding the Fund, for the financial year to which it relates:
 (a) a balance sheet of assets and liabilities; and
 (b) a comprehensive income and expenditure statement.

33 Annual Audit
 (1) The audit of the Fund by the Auditor General under Section 42(3) of the Act
 shall be performed in accordance with the Audit Act 1973.
 (2) Members of Committees established under these Regulations shall comply
 with any direction by the auditor to provide information, explanation, or
 assistance in connection with the audit.
 (3) Agreements between the Fund and an international organisation may
 specify additional audit requirements.

 PART 5 — GRANT ADMINISTRATION AND PROJECT APPLICATIONS

 34 Calls for Proposals
 (1) The Managing Committee shall issue an annual Call for Proposals once it
 determines that there are sufficient funds in the Operations Account of the
 Fund.
 (2) The Call for Proposals may include priority themes identified in the most
 recent national action plan relating to climate change or environment
 protection approved by the Cabinet.
 (3) The Chief Administrative Officer shall ensure that a Call for Proposals is
 published:
 (a) in the Government Gazette; and
 (b) in a manner that is accessible to members of the public in Naoero.

 35 Categories of Grant
 (1) The Managing Committee may establish categories of grant for funding
 through the Call for Proposals.
 (2) The categories of grant pursuant to subregulation (1) may include small and
 large grant programs.
 (3) Small grants funded through the Call for Proposals shall not be substantial
 development projects for the purposes of the Act.
 (4) The Guidelines shall set out rules and procedures for grant applications
 under this Regulation, including where appropriate for small and large grant
 programs.

 36 Eligibility for Grants
 (1) The following are eligible to apply for grants under this Part:
 (a) citizens of Naoero;
 (b) Departments or Agencies of the Government of Naoero;
 (c) public enterprises in Naoero as defined in the Public Enterprises Act
 2019; and
 (d) non-governmental organisations or community-based organisations
 with a representative office in Naoero.
 (2) Eligible applicants may partner with, or receive co-financing from,
 international organisations in applications for funding under this Part.
 (3) Applicants for grants under this Part shall provide proof of eligibility in
 accordance with subregulation (1).

 37 Criteria for Evaluation
 (1) The Technical Working Committee shall evaluate grant applications under
 this Part according to the following criteria:
 (a) alignment with priority themes set out in the Call for Proposals;
 (b) alignment with purposes of the Fund under the Act and these
 Regulations;

 (c) alignment with national plans, strategies and policies approved by
 Cabinet relating to climate change and environment protection;
 (d) cost-effectiveness of the proposal with reference to project objectives
 and budget;
 (e) the capacity of the applicant to implement the project and meet project
 objectives;
 (f) the capacity of the applicant to meet reporting and record-keeping
 requirements under this Part;
 (g) complementarity of the proposal with other projects funded by the
 Treasury Fund or Development Fund of Naoero;
 (h) protection of vulnerable persons, including women, children, and the
 disabled; and
 (i) compliance with Environmental and Social Safeguards as set out in the
 Guidelines, or in Agreements between the Fund and international
 organisations.
 (2) The Managing Committee shall approve or reject applications under this
 Part in accordance with the criteria set out in subregulation (1).

38 Project Applications
 (1) The Chief Administrative Officer shall collate grant applications under this
 Part for evaluation by a Technical Working Committee.
 (2) The Technical Working Committee shall provide written recommendations
 on grant applications under this Part to the Managing Committee.
 (3) Written recommendations under subregulation (2) shall be provided:
 (a) within 2 months of the receipt of grant applications under this Part; or
 (b) at a date to be set by resolution of the Managing Committee.
 (4) The Managing Committee shall reject or approve grant applications under
 this Part within 1 month of receipt of written recommendations from the
 Technical Working Committee.
 (5) The Managing Committee shall:
 (a) take into account the recommendations of the Technical Working
 Committee; and
 (b) provide reasons in writing within 7 days in the event of failure to
 follow recommendations Technical Working Committee.
 (6) The Managing Committee shall provide a list of approved projects to the
 Department of Finance and the Cabinet.

39 Project Implementation
 (1) The Managing Committee shall enter into project implementation
 agreements with successful grant applicants under this Part on behalf of the
 Fund.
 (2) A project implementation agreement under subregulation (1) shall include:
 (a) names of the parties;
 (b) description of the project;
 (c) date of commencement of implementation;
 (d) project work schedule and deliverables;
 (e) monitoring, evaluation and verification measures;
 (f) reporting requirements; and

 (g) a grievance redress mechanism.
 (3) A successful grant applicant under this Part shall provide the following
 project implementation reports:
 (a) quarterly financial and implementation reports; and
 (b) a project completion report with consolidated financial statements.
 (4) Project implementation reports under subregulation (3) shall include
 monitoring, evaluation, and reporting mechanisms as set out in the
 Guidelines.
 (5) The Guidelines shall set out prescribed forms for project reporting.

 40 Suspension or Termination of Funding
 The Managing Committee may choose to suspend or terminate funding for a
 project under this Part in the event of non-compliance with the project
 implementation agreement, or any other obligation imposed by the Act, these
 Regulations or any other written law.

 41 Monitoring, Evaluation and Verification
 (1) The Chief Administrative Officer shall be responsible for monitoring,
 evaluating and verifying projects under this Part in accordance with
 procedures set out in the Guidelines.
 (2) The Chief Administrative Officer shall provide an annual monitoring,
 evaluation, and verification report on projects under this Part to the
 Managing Committee.
 (3) The Managing Committee shall include monitoring, evaluation, and
 verification outcomes in the annual report provided to the Supervisory
 Committee.

 42 Grievance Redress Mechanism
 The Managing Committee shall approve a grievance redress mechanism to be
 set out in the Guidelines.
